main_result.title: A predeclared five-component lambda portfolio cuts worst-case rare-mismatch certification regret by about 41% relative to the existing uniform eight-component mixture while provably avoiding regressions on a declared 306-scenario binary design envelope.

design_envelope.decision: first time the anytime-valid upper endpoint for average conditional mismatch is <= tolerance

placement_reduction.result: For a fixed number k of mismatches, front-loading all mismatches is worst-case for first-certification delay among permutations of those outcomes.
placement_reduction.reason: At fixed tolerance and time, every lambda component and therefore their fixed mixture is nonincreasing in cumulative mismatch score. A front-loaded path has weakly larger cumulative mismatch count at every prefix than any delayed permutation, so it cannot cross earlier. This removes an early-vs-late placement tuning degree of freedom for this specific first-crossing objective.

main_result.likelihood_ratio_interpretation: For binary Y and candidate tolerance m, one component exp(-lambda*k)/(1-m(1-exp(-lambda)))^t equals the Bernoulli likelihood ratio of a lower mismatch alternative q=m*exp(-lambda)/(1-m+m*exp(-lambda)) against m. For rare m, q/m is approximately exp(-lambda), so a lambda mixture is interpretable as a portfolio over fractions of the tolerated mismatch burden.

broad_no_regression_portfolio.interpretation: Within the declared 306 binary scenarios, the optimized portfolio crosses no later than the baseline and reduces worst excess delay from about 28.18% over the per-scenario oracle to about 16.73%.

main_result.optimization_method: For a candidate multiplicative delay R, crossing constraints are linear in mixture weights: at target time min(R*t_oracle, t_baseline), require sum_j w_j E_j >= 1/alpha for every scenario, with w_j>=0 and sum_j w_j=1. Bisection on R plus linear-program feasibility was run on a dense lambda grid, then a rounded five-component support was re-optimized under the same no-regression constraints.
external_alignment: Ryu and Wornell, Gambling-Based Confidence Sequences for Bounded Random Vectors (2024), studies mixture/universal gambling portfolios for time-uniform inference and motivates predeclared portfolio hedging.

Shekhar and Ramdas, On the near-optimality of betting confidence sets for bounded means (2023), shows betting confidence sets can approach information-theoretic limits modulo logarithmic/constant factors in their iid bounded-mean scope.
These external results do not prove this average-conditional-mean construction; validity here remains the fixed-mixture supermartingale-domination argument from the preceding role-local checkpoint.

measurement_validity_rules: Optimize a sequential certificate against a declared operational decision region rather than generic average interval width.

When an optimized mixture is selected using synthetic/public/disjoint design scenarios, freeze the portfolio before current evaluation outcomes; selecting the best portfolio after seeing current outcomes is a separate selection problem.
No-regression claims must state the finite design envelope. They do not imply dominance on fractional cluster scores, larger mismatch counts, other tolerance values, or a different estimand.

For this first-crossing objective with binary scores and fixed total mismatch count, front-loaded failures are the placement stress that matters; do not redundantly optimize early and late permutations as if they were incomparable.
A simpler fixed portfolio can beat a generic variance-adaptive CS in a low-rate deployment region without implying generic superiority for bounded-mean estimation.
scope_guards: The 306-scenario optimization is synthetic design analysis, not measured production mismatch traffic.
The no-regression result is for binary equal-cluster scores only.
Unequal cluster sizes and fractional within-cluster mismatch scores are not yet covered by the no-regression result.
The Chugg-Ramdas comparisons reuse four exact values already established in the immediately preceding own-role checkpoint; no new CR parameter was selected after outcomes.
The current default implementation was not replaced. The new portfolio remains a candidate until fractional-score and broader-robustness checks are complete.
No forbidden semantic inputs were read.

frontier.action: Benchmark the broad no-regression portfolio on fractional cluster scores and unequal cluster sizes. Keep equal-process average conditional reliability separate from request-weighted reliability; test whether the binary no-regression property survives or fails.
Replace the finite tolerance grid with a continuum or denser 0.1%-5% stress and quantify between-grid regret before promoting the portfolio into a default profile.

Build a lifetime-valid fingerprint generation/lease protocol that defaults to average-conditional-mean inference and permits stable-p inference only under an independently justified constant-mean contract.
Continue public trace search for token-to-score/sign propagation under repeated inference.

exact_next_action: Stress the candidate lambda portfolio on fractional per-process mismatch scores and unequal process sizes, with separate equal-process and request-weighted estimands, before changing any default mixture.
